headline: Maritime Expert Advises Installing Speed Bumps on High Seas to Ensure Safer Navigation for Seafarers
body:
Q: With recent discussions at the BRICS Summit focusing on the safety of international waters, what is your primary proposal for the safety of our seafarers?

A: It is quite simple, really. We have successfully implemented speed bumps on almost every street in urban India to manage traffic, and there is no logical reason why we cannot apply this same technology to the Indian Ocean. My team suggests deploying a series of floating, reinforced-rubber speed bumps at strategic intervals along major shipping lanes.

Q: Wouldn't these bumps be a major hazard for large cargo vessels trying to navigate narrow straits?

A: Not at all! If a ship hits a bump at 20 knots, it is forced to slow down to a crawl to avoid internal damage to its cargo. This effectively makes the entire ocean a 'no-speeding' zone, which aligns perfectly with the diplomatic sentiment of ensuring safer passage. We are currently looking for a partner to manufacture these bumps in high-visibility neon yellow.

Q: How do you plan to address the logistical challenge of anchoring these bumps to the ocean floor at such significant depths?

A: That is a detail for the engineering subcommittee to resolve, but we are optimistic. We believe that if we make the bumps heavy enough—perhaps by filling them with discarded shipping containers—they will stay in place. It is a win-win for everyone involved in the current maritime safety dialogue.
caption: New proposal at the BRICS Summit: Speed bumps for the high seas to keep our ships moving at a 'civilized' pace. Finally, a solution that actually gets traffic moving—or rather, stops it entirely! #BRICS2026 #MaritimeSafety #Logistics (satire)
igHook: Would you trust a ship navigating over a speed bump in the middle of the ocean?
